title: Book 11 opens: priesthood; legal type of priesthood in Christ
english: ON ADORATION AND WORSHIP IN SPIRIT AND TRUTH — BOOK ELEVEN. Concerning priesthood, and that according to law it was a type of the one in Christ.

Cyril: Concerning the tent at least and the things oracled upon it, a word sufficient for us very well and gracefully polished unto spiritual thinness has been finished. And it would be fitting, as at least it seems to me—and you yourself also will somehow agree, I know—to take hold of the honors of priesthood, and again in what manner through the one in type and according to law the true is signified—that is, the one in Christ and through him sanctifying the sacred race, and I mean again those who have been flashed in faith, and who have been enriched with intimacy unto God, through at least having shared holy Spirit.
Palladius: For it would be fitting and very reasonably.

Cyril: So then with the holy tent having been completed in fitting beauty, and having been brought into the form shown on the mountain to all-divine Moses, God was making the showing-forth of the priests, and indeed also was saying, ‘And you bring toward yourself both Aaron your brother and his sons from
translator_notes: Ends mid into §2 sons of Israel; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Named call to priesthood; Aaron type of Christ; Moses must draw Aaron near
english: Cyril: …of the sons of Israel to priest for me, Aaron and Nadab and Abihu, and Eleazar, and Ithamar sons of Aaron.’ So then by name the chosen have been called toward sacred-work. ‘For no one takes the honor for himself, but the one being called by God,’ according to what has been written. So then let no one go self-chosen unto priesting for God, but let him wait a call, or if attempting to snatch what he does not have by the votes from above, he will undergo the justice of Dathan and Abiram. And do not marvel if the self-chosen among us is outlandish and unbeautiful, when also concerning Christ himself Paul writes, ‘He did not glorify himself to become high priest, but the one who spoke toward him, You are a priest unto the age according to the order of Melchizedek.’ So then of the call the one said upon Christ an image again would be the wisely said toward Moses, ‘And you bring toward yourself both Aaron your brother, and his sons.’ For the, Bring toward, what else makes clear except the, Make intimate and call toward? And Christ has been called as unto high priest through counsel of the Father. And somehow with him also the all-divine disciples have been called-together and set as fellow-workers toward sacred-work. Therefore also they were saying expressly, ‘For we are fellow-workers of God’; and they were going around again all the under-sun, sacred-working unto the nations the Gospel of Christ. For they have been called unto apostleship through Christ, and true is the word. But the matter was somehow altogether also willed by the Father; for one upon all the things done is the vote, because also counsel and wisdom and will of the Father is the Son. So then Aaron would be a type of Christ, and of the priesthood thought in spirit and truth, as it were a pre-showing-forth, as still in the dimmer shadows. And understand that Moses is ordered to bring toward himself Aaron; for somehow weak and incomplete is the law, even if it should be put apart from Christ. ‘For impossible for blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.’ And Christ having brought forward one sacrifice for sinners has perfected unto the continual those being sanctified. So then let those still friends of shadow and letter, and deemed worthy of Mosaic commands, know that unless they should bring toward themselves the high priest and apostle of our confession Jesus the Christ, unto nothing for them will the zeal of the worship in type finish. For what boasts would there be beside the virtue-loving God of the life in law? Therefore also all-wise Paul for us, through the surpassing of the knowledge of Christ, says to think dung the things in world, and to choose instead the spiritual things; and this is intelligibly the bringing toward himself Aaron himself.
Palladius: I understand what you say; for clear is the word.
Cyril: Bring toward yourself then, he says,

title: Aaron helps weak Moses; priestly garments = put on Christ
english: Cyril: …Aaron your brother, and according to another manner, I think, knowing the matter not unhelpful unto benefit as in spiritual thinking; and understand what I say. For Moses was being sent, leading Israel out from the misery in Egypt. Then seeing the attempt standing far beyond human power, and beyond measures of the strength and eloquence present for him, he was entreating saying: ‘Behold I am not well-spoken before yesterday, nor before the third, nor from when you began to speak to your attendant; thin-voiced and slow-tongued am I.’ And with God toward these saying, ‘Who gave a mouth to a human? who made hard-of-hearing and deaf, seeing and blind? Did not I Lord God? And now go, and I will open your mouth.’ Being worsted by the superiority of the achievements he was fearing again, and indeed was saying, ‘I beg, Lord, appoint another, the one able, whom you will send.’ And God was appointing at that time at once Aaron, unto a type of Christ who knows how to set upright all things easily; and Israel has been ransomed not otherwise, unless as a fellow-worker for Moses’ thin-speech and weakness again, as in an image in Aaron, Christ has been given; thus also here you will think. For perfecting the weak of the law in Christ, he brought Aaron alongside unto priesthood, and joins him usefully to blessed Moses. For neither unto ransom would the law suffice, nor indeed unto being able to perfect unto sanctification those who have been ransomed. And ransom and sanctification is Christ, with saints working-together; just as indeed Moses with Aaron in Egypt then, and with Aaron himself the sons. And with the high priest and leader of all, Christ, the all-divine disciples were also working-together intelligibly. Not running together as with one weak, though being able to set upright all things, but as having been called toward service and chosen by merit, and gaining from him the well-strong upon all. And all-divine Paul will witness saying: ‘I am strong for all things in the Christ who empowers me.’
Palladius: So then chosen and by name have Aaron and the rest been called toward sacred-liturgy.

Cyril: And in addition to these at least he was legislating bright and priest-fitting garments to be constructed for them saying: ‘And you will make a holy stole for Aaron your brother unto honor and glory, and you speak to all the wise in understanding, whom I have filled with spirit of sense, and they will make the holy stole of Aaron unto the holy, in which he will priest for me.’ So then all-wise Paul advises those justified in faith that the truly holy and from-heaven stole must be put on writing: ‘Put on our Lord Jesus Christ.’ For this indeed the prophet Isaiah has cried beforehand saying as from person of the Church, ‘Let my soul rejoice upon the Lord, for he has put on me a garment of salvation and a tunic of gladness.’ So then a garment the unto

title: Christ the garment of honor; gold/purple/linen/scarlet/hyacinth = Word’s glory
english: Cyril: …honor and glory truly for the sacred and holy race is Christ, a bright and beyond-world adornment for the souls of the saints. ‘For as many as into Christ you were baptized, Christ you put on,’ he says, and true is the word. And as in shadows the law beautifies Aaron, carrying up unto Christ the glory from having been dressed many-formedly. For all but also woven-together with the construction of the craft-works a mystical and exact word is found, showing riddlingly the glory of the Savior. For see how he says the craftsmen of the garments have been filled with the understanding from God, carrying them unto flower-bright embroidery, and writing the glory of Christ into the robes. And breastpiece and shoulder-piece, and foot-reaching robe, and the tasseled tunic, and headdress and belt, the things being crafted, these and in addition to them others, which also part by part for us, as possible, will be said. So then he said concerning those taken into the works, ‘And they will take the gold, and the hyacinth, and the purple, and the scarlet, and linen.’ And again casting a thin mind into the things set forth for me, and before at least the others observe this.
Palladius: What sort of thing do you say?
Cyril: For have not of gold and linen, and indeed also purple and spun scarlet, and hyacinth again all the things in the tent been made, and it was unto a type of Christ?
Palladius: Thus it holds.

Cyril: And see that through the same also the stole of the one excelling in priesthood has been arranged, travailing the glory of Christ as again in an image and types; for the same words, and not another knowledge, signify the beauty of Christ. For he is known as in gold God, as in purple having the kingly dignity, and as in fine linen a thin and bodiless word, as in scarlet through the flesh; and in air-appearing hyacinth—for such-colored is hyacinth—through the from-above and from heaven. Or is not the Word from God Father both God together and king?
Palladius: How not?
Cyril: And being Word of the Father thin and bodiless, has he not come to be in flesh and is he from above?
Palladius: True.

Cyril: So then the same materials indistinguishably and as in thin contemplation both of the garments, and indeed also of the things constructed in the holy tent. And these things thus; and the things unto honor and glory for Aaron many-formedly woven it is already time to say. So then, ‘And they will make,’ he says, ‘the shoulder-piece from spun linen, a woven work of an embroiderer, two shoulder-pieces holding together will be for him, one the other upon the two parts having been hung. And the weave of the
notes_covered: gold God; purple king; linen Word; scarlet flesh; hyacinth heaven

title: Ephod emerald stones = Israel on Christ’s shoulders; heaven-colored memorial
english: Cyril: …shoulder-pieces, which is upon it according to the making, from it will be from gold and hyacinth and purple and scarlet spun-through and spun linen.’ And having given the material already said beforehand to the weaves, at once he adds: ‘And you will take the two stones, emerald stones, and you will engrave in them the names of the sons of Israel, six names about the one stone, and the six remaining names upon the second stone, according to their births, a work of stone-working craft; an engraving of a seal you will engrave the stones upon the names of the sons of Israel. And you will set the two stones upon the shoulders of the shoulder-piece; stones of memorial are they for the sons of Israel.’
Palladius: Deep, as it seems, is the word in the contemplations; and try first to say that, what is the matter of the so-called shoulder-piece, or what manner of construction it would have.

Cyril: He has ordered some weave as in form of a tunic and reaching as far as the chest to come to be, as having been brought upon the garments themselves inward and as on skin and as far as feet, and flashing the ray from gold and purple, it would birth for the eyes of those watching a solemn and priest-fitting marvel. This he has called shoulder-piece, through, I think, the short of the craft-work, and the barely stretching upon both shoulders. So then in this shoulder-piece two stones—and these of emerald—well bound with thin threads he was clearly typing must be fixed, with the tribes having been dug-in artfully by name, so that six be written in one stone. And what is the word of this, he himself was clarifying for us saying: ‘And Aaron will take the names of the sons of Israel opposite Lord upon his two shoulders, a memorial concerning them.’
Palladius: And what again through the stones and the things in them will we think to be hinted?

Cyril: Hear then; pale is the emerald stone. And the ray-formed is swimming in it in depth, and as it were light has been mixed with dark; each dragging the conquering toward itself. So then, O Palladius, looking toward the high and above, the eye of the body, and straining unto the deep toward aether and heaven, will it not cast forward some such contemplation? for pale somehow and as in depth black, and mixed with moderate light, is the uppermost aether.
Palladius: Thus it holds.

Cyril: So then an image of heaven the sacred Letter makes the stone. And do not marvel when also with sapphire it likens it again. For pale is the sapphire, and not far from the sight in emerald. And it has been written thus in the Exodus, ‘And Moses and Aaron went up, and Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the eldership of Israel. And they saw the place where the God of Israel had stood; and the things under his feet, as a work of sapphire stone, and as form of firmament of the heaven, in the cleanness.’
translator_notes: Ends at Exod 24 quote; Egypt idolatry continues §6.

title: Heaven under God’s feet; names in heaven on Christ; breastpiece of judgments begins
english: Cyril: For since having come to be in Egypt those from Israel have served the creation, and were calling heaven god, usefully the Lord of the wholes was also appearing having stepped upon the firmament itself, that they might know that he has all things under feet, and is master of the heavens themselves, as craftsman. So then you understand that as some type and imaging of heaven the sacred Letter makes the stone pale-ing as in moderate light? for blue-rayed by nature.
Palladius: You have spoken most excellently.

Cyril: So then a sign of heaven is the emerald, having Israel written according to race, and having obtained as place the shoulder-piece, through which it will be present to think, that whoever should be those who have obtained the registration in heaven, these altogether and wholly will rest upon Christ, all but also having them upon shoulders, and making the good as in an order of children. And such also the divine Moses said, beautifying Israel with the sparing from God: ‘As an eagle should shelter its nest, and upon its nestlings it yearned, spreading its wings it received them, and took them up upon its mid-backs.’ But somehow also David sings for every holy one, and one having dwelt in help of the Highest, ‘Upon his mid-backs he will overshadow you,’ he says. Mid-backs somehow as I myself think the under-neck parts, and the as in shoulders hinting, and not altogether the backs. So then upon shoulders they will be lifted, according to the prophet’s voice, and upon arm they will be taken up according to the ancient Ephraim, those who have obtained the above registration, which as well-famed and worthy-of-marvel and lying-above the beauty of the divine gifts the Savior himself has declared, saying thus to the holy disciples: ‘Do not rejoice that the demons are subjected to you, but rejoice rather that your names have been written in the heavens.’ And he says the registration at least in the stones will be a memorial for the sons of Israel opposite Lord, all but also of one gazing-intently, as in Aaron; for God and Father receives us unto remembrance in Christ, and we have become in him both known and worthy of oversight, and as in a book of God.
Palladius: You have spoken uprightly.

Cyril: And another adornment he orders must be brought alongside for this saying, ‘And you will make little shields from pure gold having been mixed, and you will make two tassels from pure gold having been mixed in flowers a work of plaiting, and you will set the plaited tassels upon the little shields and their shoulder-straps from the front things. And you will make an oracle of the judgments, a work of a weaver according to the rhythm of the shoulder-piece, you will make it from gold and hyacinth, and purple and spun scarlet, and spun linen, you will make it square, it will be double of a span the length and of a span the breadth, And you will weave in it a weave according to the
notes_covered: Egypt served creation; God above firmament

title: Twelve breastpiece stones; construction of oracle; why ‘oracle of judgments’
english: Cyril: …four-rowed stone.’ Then having composed the names of the stones, he adds again, ‘And the stones will be from the names of the sons of Israel twelve, according to their names, engravings of seals of each according to their names will be unto the twelve tribes.’ And next after a few: ‘And Aaron will take,’ he says, ‘the names of the sons of Israel upon the oracle of the judgment, upon the chest when entering into the Holy, a memorial opposite Lord God.’
Palladius: How deep the matter of the oracle, and altogether hard-to-reach even the manner of the construction seems to me to be.

Cyril: So then one must go upon them, and as very near the truth, even if the steepness does not perhaps allow to reach it altogether. For to see the very unclear things even at least in a mirror, I myself would say differs from the other—I mean from not having been thought at all. So then I will say, as possible and as I would have according to mind. He has ordered two little shields to come to be from pure gold, broader than according to a circle of a coin, yet in the same form; for circular is the coin; then two tassels mixed in flowers from pure gold. And we say the tassels are chains, having the sight as in colors having been varied. For he said flowers the colors. And linen then was also purple these, and a golden thread, and indeed also hyacinth, and the scarlet twist. And in addition to this at least he says a square weave must come to be, and as in form of a cube, span-measured, equal-sided everywhere. And he says the twelve stones must be woven in it very well, and lying three each, as in four whole rows with the tribes having been carved in them by name. So then from the shoulder-piece, the little shields having been hung with golden and many-formed chains were sitting under gently, seeming both high and to be upon the shoulders themselves. And they were touching the chests and already were hanging upon the breasts themselves; and from at least the little shields with other chains the oracle of the judgments well fastened was floating upon the chest, with tassels having been hung. And the matter was not unmarvelous for those seeing, translucent with stones and gold and with the good-colors of the other materials having been worked all-gloriously. And this again will be unto remembrance for the sons of Israel, opposite Lord when Aaron enters into the Holy. So then is the shape of the craft-works clear for you as possible now?
Palladius: And very much. And instead of what then the name oracle of the judgments for the craft-work?
Cyril: For have we not also said etymologizing that the upper has been called shoulder-piece, through having been stretched upon both shoulders?
Palladius: Yes. What then is this at least?
Cyril: That again etymologically and proportionally the as

title: Oracle on heart = right judgment; saints as precious stones; arms of righteousness
english: Cyril: …having been set away in heart and inwards we say has been named oracle of the judgments. For as a dwelling of the rational in us is heart and inwards. And as it were has been fixed and naturally planted in the rational in us also the upright and unblamable judgment upon each of the things to be practiced—that is, the righteous-judging, and what is fitting for each; for does not some rational in us weigh the natures of the things to be practiced, and separate from the better the graceless and unbeneficial?
Palladius: And altogether.

Cyril: And custom for the God-breathed Scripture is to name judgment the uprightness and righteous-judging. And indeed all-divine David sings: ‘Blessed those who keep judgment, and who do righteousness in every season.’ And he said somewhere again: ‘And honor of a king is to love judgment.’ For bright is the honor and glory of a king, loving righteousness. So then an oracle of judgment is the having been cast upon heart and chest, through as it were lying in a place of the rational, in which is the uprightness in righteousness. And in this very thing twelve stones held-around with gold, having writing, the tribes. And they would be a type of holy men, who are both bright and honored, and as some choice stones, all but also lying unto mind and heart of Christ; for they are truly worthy of memory, through at least the conspicuous in virtue, and the honored as in sanctification. And from the oracle of the judgments golden tassels also hang, the matter hinting, I think, that of the multitude of the saints the much and unnumbered swarm of achievements is all but also seen having been hung. And indeed blessed David also says the adornment of the Church is in tassels.
Palladius: Persuasive is the word.

Cyril: And from at least the oracle of the judgments a varied and good-colored chain held with golden rings creeps up, just as we were saying, and going through both little shields, reaches unto the very tip of the shoulder-piece, upon which are the stones of the registration. And what this also would be, how is it not worthy to see? So then the riddle seems to me to hint again some such thing: For as the precious stones both in knowledge and in memory of Christ, running toward the above registration, gain the matter through the weapons of righteousness of the right and left; for thus clearly all-divine Paul writes. And indeed also elsewhere he says: ‘Put on the full-armor of God.’ And golden are the king’s weapons, and golden likewise the little shields, and riddlingly showing the full-armor of God. So then we will be not otherwise in memory and registration of God, unless having grasped the weapons of righteousness, and going through them practically. And the having been fastened of the shoulder-piece
notes_covered: saints = precious stones on Christ’s heart

title: Breastpiece joins above/below; twelve stones = faith/firmness; Urim/Thummim = Christ
english: Cyril: …the oracle would signify, I think, the below having been joined to the above, with Christ mediating. ‘For he himself is our peace, the one who has made both one,’ according to the Scriptures, and having fastened the human things to the multitude of the holy angels with the bond of love. And one must know that also blessed Ezekiel says the ruler of Tyre has put on every precious stone; and he counts these, which also all-divine Moses says have been set in the oracle of the judgments. And these were, sardius, topaz, emerald, carbuncle, sapphire, and jasper, ligure, agate, amethyst, chrysolite, beryl, onyx. And they had been arranged three each, and in whole four rows, the such placing sketching for us the firm in faith of those in heart and memory of Christ. For of faith is the three each, and as in Trinity a symbol; and of firmness the as in a square and equal-sided shape. For thus the oracle had been made, upon which also the twelve stones.
Palladius: I am persuaded.

Cyril: And in addition to these at least he orders also something else to be woven-together with the twelve stones, saying: ‘And you will set upon the oracle of the judgment the disclosure and the truth, and it will be upon the chest of Aaron, when he enters into the Holy opposite Lord, and Aaron will bring in the judgments of the sons of Israel upon the chest opposite Lord through all.’ So then he names disclosure and truth, yet he has not still also made clear distinctly whether stones, or as on a small tablet a writing he has ordered to come to be. And I will remember a prophet saying, ‘Because for many days the sons of Israel will sit, there not being a king, nor a ruler, there not being a sacrifice, nor there being an altar, nor a priesthood, nor disclosures.’ But whether these also should be stones, or as on a golden tablet a writing of the names, the word will not investigate very much, and we will know they have been set unto a type, of Christ being present with saints. ‘For behold,’ he says, ‘I am with you all the days, and until completion of the age.’ And truth and disclosure is Christ. For in him we have known the Father, and he has disclosed for us his good will the perfect and well-pleasing, according to the Scriptures. For somewhere Christ said: ‘No longer do I say you slaves, you are my friends, because all things which I heard from my Father I announced to you.’ And truth also otherwise is Emmanuel, because he alone by nature is Son, and as from God God, alone holy, alone Lord; and by participation is the creation, and according to imitation, as many as he himself is thought to be. So then Christ is present with the saints as being thought in disclosure and truth, who also in person of the Father brings in the things according to us, always living unto the interceding for us. For this, I think, is the, And Aaron will bring in the judgments of the sons of Israel
translator_notes: Ends mid into §10 upon chest always.

title: Hyacinth robe = above immortality; pomegranates/bells = Gospel economy entry
english: Cyril: …opposite Lord upon his chest through all.
Palladius: True.

Cyril: And a priest-fitting and worthy-of-marvel garment he orders must be constructed saying: ‘And you will make an under-garment foot-reaching, wholly hyacinth, and the mouth-around will be from it middle, having a hem in a circle of the mouth-around, a work of a weaver, the joining woven-together from it, that it may not be torn. And you will make under the border of the under-garment below, as of a pomegranate flowering pomegranate-lets from hyacinth, and purple, and scarlet spun-through, and spun linen, under the border of the under-garment in a circle. The same form for the pomegranate-lets, and golden bells in midst of these in a circle beside a golden pomegranate-bell, and flowered upon the border of the under-garment in a circle. And Aaron when liturgizing, his voice will be audible, when entering into the Holy opposite Lord, and when going out, that he may not die.’ So then under-garment and foot-reaching, a long tunic, both well-formed toward wrapping-around, and the going from the neck itself unto extreme feet, he names clearly; and from hyacinth, because a symbol of the above immortality—that is, of Christ. For such indeed also all-divine David has announced beforehand saying as from person of God concerning those sacred-working in the churches: ‘Her priests I will put on salvation.’ Put on our Lord Jesus Christ, also wise Paul charges us. And this, I think, is our dwelling the from heaven, which we yearn to put on, the tunic of gladness, the garment of the salvation, according to the prophet’s voice. And a type of heaven is the hyacinth color said clearly. And true is the word, as upon us ourselves. For we have been wrapped with the immortality from above. And if also Christ himself should be thought, as in Aaron having the foot-reaching under-garment, no less true for us is the word; for being God by nature the Only-begotten, he finishes his own body incorruptible, and having wrapped it with the life from above, he was somehow altogether setting it in better things than the greed of death; for that both naturally together and unparticipatedly in Christ are both immortality and life, you will understand also from here. For he said as indeed also existing by nature God, ‘I am the resurrection and the life.’ And being life-made according to the human, ‘For just as the Father,’ he says, ‘has life in himself, so also to the Son he has given to have life in himself.’ So then even if Christ himself should be thought, the one said to have been wrapped with the immortality from above, the word would not go out from the fitting. And in addition at least to the below parts perhaps, pomegranate-lets and bells alternating the things lying in; and pomegranate-lets as woven-together, and golden the bells; that they might be well-sounding according to the true, and indeed also when Aaron runs into the Holies of holies, they make his running-in most notable. And this also is a symbol of the saving and wise economy—I mean of the divine and Gospel
translator_notes: Ends mid κηρύγματος into §11; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Bells = Gospel; pomegranates = cities; gold plate = Holy to Lord / Son sent
english: Cyril: …proclamation, as it were buzzing around every city, when for us the great high priest, the unblemished victim, has entered into the Holies of holies, having found age-long ransom. ‘For by one offering he has perfected unto the continual those being sanctified.’ And a not unclear riddle as it were: of the saving proclamation the bells having come to be from gold, and of cities the pomegranate-lets.
Palladius: In what manner?

Cyril: For as a city is bound outside with one wall, and holds within itself countless households; in the same manner, I think, also the matter of the pomegranate is girded outside with one rind, and within the seeds are walled from one another with thin coats, and all but are gathered according to households. Or does it not hold thus?
Palladius: I agree.

Cyril: So then a bell beside each pomegranate; for a teacher beside each city, by the ringing-out and good-sound of the divine dogmas, setting clear for all the running-in of our Savior into the Holies of holies. And a fear has also been hung over, that he may not die—clearly if speechless and without the Gospel sound someone should dare the sacred things. And upon the headdress a gold leaf he orders to be bound, engraved Seal of holiness of Lord. And this is a type of the kingship and sending of Christ; for having been sanctified and sent into the world he himself says toward Jews: ‘If those it called gods toward whom the word of God came, and the Scripture cannot be loosed, of whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, do you say that You blaspheme, because I said, I am Son of God?’ So then when the Son says himself to have been sanctified by God and Father, he makes clear the as-it-were having been chosen-beforehand and sent. So then a holy-thing of Lord, he says, this is, a showing-forth unto this world and
notes_covered: Exod 28 gold plate Holy to Lord

title: Mitre hyacinth = heavenly kingdom; linen war-gear of priesthood
english: Cyril: …sending, yet unto kingdom and glory. For thus he perfects Aaron, setting the golden plate upon the forehead. And Lord of the wholes and king is Christ, both naturally together and by participation. For being God by nature he has emptied himself, having come down in a slave’s form. And he receives kingdom, according at least to what is fitting for the human shape, though from above and from beginning sitting-with God and Father, and co-ruling the wholes and co-master. And understand how from hyacinth his mitre has come to be, having the bright signal of the kingdom—I mean the golden leaf. And hyacinth is a sign of heaven; and remember Christ saying, ‘My kingdom is not from this world.’ For not an earthly king, but heavenly is Christ, having all the creation under feet. And having added, that ‘And Aaron will take away the sins of the holy things, as many as they should sanctify, of every gift of their holy things,’ that every approach and perfection is in Christ, he has made clear… And Christ ‘in a hidden hand,’ according to what has been written, and ‘His bow he has stretched, and prepared it, his arrows for those being burned he has worked out,’ and he has taken down rulers, has triumphed over powers, has shaken lordships, and has rescued those upon the earth being captives. And that the war has not become visible or thick for him, nor such as toward blood and flesh, the warlike gear having come to be from linen alone the very
notes_covered: Eph 6 not flesh/blood; linen war kit

title: Sons’ tunics/girdles; linen trousers; consecrate with calf and rams
english: Cyril: …thin has the warlike gear come to be, both headdress and belt. So then with a priest-fitting adornment he shows Aaron bright and worthy-of-marvel. And he orders further saying: ‘And for the sons of Aaron you will make tunics and belts, and headdresses you will make for them unto honor and glory. And you will put them on Aaron your brother, and his sons with him. And you will anoint them, and fill their hands, and sanctify them, that they may priest for me. And you will make for them linen trousers to cover shame of their skin, from loin until thighs it will be. And Aaron will have them and his sons, when they enter into the tent of the testimony, or when they approach to liturgize toward the altar of the holy. And they will not bring sin upon themselves, that they may not die. An age-long lawful thing for him and for his seed after him.’ You see that also for those from Aaron themselves it is fitting to be seen as at least in the warlike shape. For fight-ready is the sacred race altogether…

Cyril: Thus it holds; and with such a stole he beautifies the sacred and chosen race, and sanctifies also otherwise, as still in shadow, yet in Christ. For it has been written thus: ‘And these are what you will do for them, to sanctify them so as for them to priest for me: you will take one calf from cattle, and two unblemished rams, and unleavened breads mixed in oil, and unleavened cakes anointed in oil. Fine flour from wheat

title: Wash, vest, anoint; hands on calf; blameless hands and pure heart
english: Cyril: …you will make them, and you will set them upon one basket, and you will bring them forward upon the basket, and the calf, and the two rams. And Aaron and his sons you will bring forward upon the doors of the tent of the testimony, and you will wash them in water. And taking the stoles, you will put on Aaron your brother both the foot-reaching tunic, and the shoulder-piece, and the oracle. And you will join for him the oracle toward the shoulder-piece. And you will set the mitre upon his head, and you will set the leaf the holy-thing upon the mitre, and you will take of the oil of the anointing, and you will pour it upon his head, and you will anoint him. And his sons you will bring forward, and you will put tunics on them, and you will gird them with the belts, and you will put around them the headdresses. And priesthood for me will be for them unto the age, and you will perfect Aaron’s hands, and the hands of his sons.’ So then he has ordered a calf and two rams to be brought forward unto sacrifice… And of the one about to approach God: ‘Innocent in hands and pure in heart.’
Palladius: It seems so.

Cyril: And in what manner again the sacrifices for the priests must be exacted, he was legislating saying: ‘And you will bring forward the calf upon the doors of the tent of the testimony, and Aaron and his sons will set their hands upon the head of the calf opposite Lord, beside the doors of the tent of the testimony, and you will slaughter the calf opposite Lord, beside the

title: Sin-calf burned outside; ram whole-burnt; ram of perfection / wave portions
english: Cyril: …doors of the tent of the testimony. And you will take from the blood of the calf, and you will set upon the two horns of the altar with your finger. And all the remaining blood you will pour out beside the base of the altar, and you will take all the fat upon the belly, and the lobe upon the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat upon them, and you will set upon the altar. And the meats of the calf, and the skin, and the dung you will burn with fire outside the camp; for it is of sin. And the one ram you will take, and Aaron and his sons will set their hands upon the head of the ram, and you will slaughter it, and taking the blood you will pour toward the altar in a circle, and you will divide the ram according to limbs; and you will wash the inwards and the feet with water, and you will set upon the divided-parts with the head, and you will bring up the whole ram upon the altar, a whole-burnt-offering to the Lord unto a smell of fragrance; it is incense to Lord. And you will take… and what has been removed from the ram of the perfection from Aaron and from his sons, and it will be for Aaron and for his sons an age-long lawful thing from the sons of Israel; for this is a setting-apart, and a removal it will be from the sons of Israel from the victims of the salvations of the sons of Israel, a removal to Lord.’ And after a few: ‘And the ram of the perfection you will take, and you will boil the meats in a holy place, and Aaron and
translator_notes: Ends mid sons will eat into §16.

title: Priestly meal holy; Christ sanctifies many ways; calf fat virtues; suffered outside
english: Cyril: …his sons will eat the meats of the ram, and the breads in the basket, beside the doors of the tent of the testimony they will eat them, in which they were sanctified in them to perfect their hands to sanctify them, and a foreigner will not eat from them; for they are holy. And if from the meats of the sacrifice of the perfection and of the breads should be left until morning, you will burn the remaining things with fire. It will not be eaten; for it is a holy-thing.’
Palladius: How deep the matter of the legal commands.

Cyril: Deep indeed very much; for you have spoken uprightly; yet not altogether unclear, with the divine light of the holy Spirit flashing in us. And come then again, as possible, let us say the things upon each. In countless manners our Lord Jesus Christ sanctifies us, and finishes us sacred and well-acceptable. For through him and in him we have had the approach, and we are not unwanted to God and Father. And most needful and necessary unto salvation for us under corruption and sin are both… which also would be unto a type of the virtues unto the inward and unto mind, in which is the fragrant spiritually, yet not according to one manner, since indeed many are the inwards, fat and kidneys, and the lobe of the liver. And the remaining of the body is burned, outside the camp. For outside the gate Christ has suffered; and Paul writes thus. And the being spent with fire of the body would signify thinly, that the passion for him and the

title: Death unto glory like Sinai fire; first ram = life offered; Adam’s curse reversed
english: Cyril: …death will not be somehow unto dishonor, but will finish out unto bright and most manifest glory. For in a form at least of fire the divine is thought; and thus it has also come down upon the mountain Sinai. And about to loose the power of death, Christ has entered under death economically, that as God he may be glorified by us. So then the death creeps unto God-fitting glory, having as end the bright living-again, and the small-fitting in the suffering, being conquered by the uppermost good-fames, goes away unto nothing; and this, I think, is riddlingly the being spent with fire of the dead calf. And having added, that for it is sin, he has made clear that the passion of Christ has come to be unto cleansing-off of sin, and the matter is not unclear.
Palladius: Not at all.

Cyril: Then the first ram is taken and is slaughtered equally with the calf; and the blood again was being held toward the altar, and being cut limb-wise was being brought up, with the inwards having been washed with water, with head together and feet…
Palladius: And would someone think perhaps that even the life of Christ itself has come to be for us?

Cyril: And indeed you will know somehow also very easily, having thought that we have become sharers of the transgression in Adam, and all but have also paid the justices of the things failed by that one, with the curse having run through unto all, and the anger having somehow been distributed over the race from him. So then the Only-begotten has come down unto becoming-human, and has tented among us, and
notes_covered: Sinai fire = divine glory in passion
Adam curse; Word tented among us

title: Obedient unto death; second ram blood on ear/hand/foot; test the spirits
english: Cyril: …has subjected himself to God and Father. ‘For he has become obedient until death,’ wiping out the charges of the from-Adam desertion, and of the well-persuadedness the fragrance as for all together and for each he has brought forward to God and Father, and through him we have been saved; and witness is Paul having written thus: ‘So then, as through one trespass unto all humans unto condemnation, so also through one righteous-deed unto all humans unto justification of life; for just as through the disobedience of the one human the many were set down sinners, so through the obedience of the one human the many will be set down righteous.’ So then you understand that we have been saved as at least in the calf, with Christ having died for us, and we are fragrant to God and Father through his subjection and the life in sanctification; for the blood of the ram was being held toward the holy altar.
Palladius: I understand what you say.

Cyril: And many-manneredly molding the same for us as in shadows: And you will take, he says, the second ram… fighting, and leading-out against the dogmas of uprightness; for this is a fruit of the holy hearing. And indeed John the all-divine somehow says thus for us: ‘Brothers, test the spirits, if it is from God; every spirit which does not confess Jesus Christ is not from God, and every spirit which confesses Jesus Christ is from God.’ And a test of words would reasonably be practiced not otherwise rather than unto an ear. So then holy

title: Ear hand foot anointed; holy food = Christ’s body; leftover burned; no alien eats
english: Cyril: …will be the ear for those caring for exactness and dogmatic uprightness. But this is Christ’s gift and heaven’s guest-gift, and an achievement of the holy blood; for of all the exceptional things for us the possession is in him and through him. Therefore also a hand was being sanctified, showing-forth of practical energy, and indeed also a foot, a clear symbol of the uprightness in tracks. For we must be solemnized with holy deeds, and walk through very well the path running through unto every one of the things pleasing God, according to what is sung in Psalms, ‘And I turned my feet unto your testimonies,’ or the in Proverbs book, ‘Make upright tracks for your feet, and straighten your roads.’ So then let the sacred and choice race possess a holy hearing, and likewise hand and foot according at least to the manners just said for us; and all right things being anointed and as in a last portion—that is, in extremes. For he says the extreme of the ear, and indeed also… For how would it be fitting for the sacred ones to come to be in participation of holy food—that is, of the body of Christ—and unapproachable for the other-born is the blessing. And other-born would also be thought the still unbelieving and unbaptized race, and in addition to these still the having been twisted unto other-minded mind, and incompatible with the judgments of the saints, and as in baseness of dogmas having been rope-separated. And with fire is also spent every leftover of the sacrifice

title: Leftover not for tomorrow; future sanctification; seven days at tent door
english: Cyril: …remainder, the law not allowing to eat also unto the tomorrow; for of sanctification, I think, some other manner will be for us according to the coming age being worked spiritually, no longer bodily, and according to which word God who rearranges all things knows, and transferring wherever he should wish. And some not unintelligent mind will follow the words; for with the corruption in us having been loosed after at least living-again perhaps from dead ones, the things through which one might be able to run-through it are somehow not necessary. So then another manner of sanctification fitting the condition of the season will be thought out, with Christ being present with us. And having said what has come unto mind, we will yield to those who think the better things. And perhaps some such thing the all-divine Paul hints saying: ‘And when the perfect should come, the from-part will be abolished,’ instead of, will have an end and will stand.
Palladius: It seems so.

Cyril: So then these things he said must be finished through unto the perfection of the sacred ones. And with the priests of Israel having been raised-together, and… and of testimony you will not go out seven days, until a day should be fulfilled, a day of your perfection. For seven days he will perfect your hands, just as he did on this day, on which Lord commanded to do, so as to propitiate concerning you, and upon the door of the tent of the testimony you will sit seven days. And day and night keep the keepings of Lord, that you may not die; for thus Lord God commanded me.’
notes_covered: seven days stay at tent door

title: Stay in tent = firmness in holiness; eighth day Moses yields to Aaron
english: Cyril: What sort of manner at least upon each of the sacrifices has come to be, a word sufficient for us has shown very well. Therefore leaving off thin-speaking at least in these, let us go upon this. The law does not allow those who have enriched a sacred and choice lot, and already perfected unto needing to priest, to be carried somewhere outside the holy tent, but unto a seventh day to sit within, and all but nails them to the doors, not overstepping the threshold, setting the sitting in holy places as a symbol, I think somehow, of firmness and remaining of the in sanctification. For we must be fixed-through and hold unshaken unto virtue necessarily, we who at least have been ordered to sit-near God, not going outside of the fitting manner and running out of a priest-fitting mind; but near as always and dwelling beside God, according at least to what has been said through a prophet’s voice: ‘Seeking seek, and beside me dwell.’ And unto seven days Moses ordered to do this; and that in every season one must sit-near God… concerning your sin, and your whole-burnt-offering, and propitiate concerning yourself, and your house, and do the gifts of the people, and propitiate concerning them, just as Lord commanded.’ Thin, O Palladius, casting the mind into the sacred Letters you will observe very well also in this the mystery of Christ clear.
Palladius: In what manner?
Cyril: For on an eighth day Moses as it were ceases from the priesting. And Aaron at least begins,

title: Eighth day = resurrection age; Christ after law; calf/ram/semolina types
english: Cyril: …yet Moses has not been silenced, though Aaron already is darting toward the works of the priesthood. For a time at least of the priesthood of Christ would reasonably be thought the after the law—that is, the eighth, according to which is the resurrection, and as some beginning of a new age. For a new creation in Christ, according to what has been written. And with Christ already having been shown-forth according to the eighth, the things of Moses cease; for we no longer worship still in types and shadows; yet at least the pedagogy in law has not been silenced, for spiritual is the law for the spiritual, and always speaks the mystery of Christ. So then Moses was announcing according to the eighth day that the glory of Lord would be seen. For the law has announced beforehand the time of our Savior’s sojourn. And he orders further again, first for Aaron to finish sacrifices for himself; and after this, those for all the people, setting the matter as a type, I think, for those according to us somehow already, and showing very well and clearly, that for those chosen unto priesthood… he shows himself for us as at least in the calf being slaughtered, and freeing from sin, and releasing from every charge, and wiping off the dirt from having been condemned, and himself likewise unto a smell of the intelligible fragrance as a ram being perfected, himself also becoming a sacrifice of salvation, and sanctifying us with his own blood, himself also fine flour oil-soaked, in cheerfulness of a holy life, showing himself for us to God and Father.

title: Emmanuel shown; priests and peoples fruit-bear; calf/lamb infancy; oil hope
english: Palladius: I understand what you say.

Cyril: And I myself think the sacrifice for Aaron and for the people gracefully hints the dedication of the saints unto God. And with Emmanuel remaining having been shown-forth and having set the things according to himself manifest, through whom we have been called unto sanctification, acceptable and sacred, and unto a smell of fragrance we have been dedicated to the Father. For observe that, through the things said just now, the perfection of the priests was being finished legally, and through him again many-manneredly of those sanctified. For he was being burned as a calf outside the camp for sin, and was being incense-burned as a ram whole-burnt fittingly, and limb-wise whole as for each and for all, was sanctifying anointing them with the blood, as a ram of salvation. And with an eighth day already remaining having been shown-forth—that is, according to which the glory of Christ has become more clear, with death having been abolished, and corruption having been trampled—remaining priests and peoples fruit-bear to God, not honoring with some foreign things, nor… And a little calf and lamb unto whole-fruit-bearing hints the in Christ infancy of those being dedicated in faith; and a calf and ram signify very well the enduring and manly, and the fruit-bearing in meekness, and of the first a type is the calf; and the ram at least of the second. And fine flour soaked with oil makes very clear the bright hope of the life in Christ; for not gloomy and tearful,

title: Cheerful polity; fire eats gifts = Spirit now; Aaron blesses; grace and peace
english: Cyril: …but cheerful and glad it is fitting to have been hung from the citizenship in Christ. For this, I think, is the, ‘Come let us rejoice to the Lord.’ For thus the glory of Christ will shine upon purely and clearly, most gladly receiving the fruit-bearings of the saints, just as indeed also then God in a form of fire has come down clearly, and has eaten up the victims. And he all but thinks food and luxury the good-repute of those sanctified in faith. And the word also hints something mystical; for then upon the divided-parts God was sending down the tip of fire, as it were somehow touching the things set forth; for the Divine always molds under itself the nature of fire. And now with the intelligible sacrifice being set before him, not in a form of fire, but in holy Spirit, touching the things set forth intelligibly, he shows life-making for those yearning to share, and we have received the matter true in faith.
Palladius: You have spoken uprightly.

Cyril: And having raised the hands Aaron blessed the people. And see again how… is for us the distributor of the heavenly goods, in him and through him all things from the Father. And indeed all-divine Paul, ‘Grace to you and peace,’ he says, ‘from God our Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ.’ So then we are blessed in name of God, and how the manner of this might perhaps come to be, signifying gracefully, he said the praying priest must voice: ‘Lord bless you and keep you,

title: Aaronic blessing = election in Christ; face of God; peace through exalted Son
english: Cyril: …Lord make his face shine upon you, and pity you, Lord lift his face upon you, and give you peace.’ So then the blessing keeps loosing the curse, and remolding the having-sinned, unto needing to be praised in Christ; and of this Paul is witness having written thus: ‘Blessed the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the one who has blessed us in every spiritual blessing, in the heavenly things in Christ, just as he chose us in him before casting-down of world, for us to be holy and unblemished before him; in love having pre-marked us unto adoption through Christ unto him.’ You see that the rejectable through the sin has fled, and the human acceptable unto adoption being blessed in Christ through participation of the Spirit, which also he has poured out unto us richly, the one not from part gifting it to the saints, but as from his own fullness putting in. And appearance of face of God would at once procure the needing to be pitied, if at least… good for those believing unto him both having set forth and gifting. ‘For peace,’ he says, ‘my peace I give you, peace my peace I leave you.’ For when as it were the Father has set the Son high, having gifted him a name the above every name, and ‘Sit from my right,’ saying, then indeed, then having loosed the enmity distancing us, we have been joined unto peace, through having chosen to think his things, and in Spirit to

title: One in Father/Son; Levites purified; ash-water = baptism / Christ’s death
english: Cyril: …walk, in whom and through whom we have been shown sharers of divine nature, with Christ stringing us unto unity; for somewhere he said toward the Father: ‘I wish that just as I and you are one, so also they in us may be one.’ ‘For one body at least we all are in Christ,’ and: ‘The one being glued to the Lord is one spirit,’ according to the Scripture. And that, with God and Father as it were lifting his own face—that is, glorifying the Son—we have been enriched with the peace toward him, he himself will clarify saying: ‘When I am lifted up from the earth, I will drag all toward myself.’
Palladius: You think uprightly. ‘For he himself is our peace, and through him we have had the approach in spirit toward the Father.’

Cyril: So then concerning priests and the showing-forth upon them these things the law toward us. And that the Levitical must be sanctified very well he says, and having been pre-purified with the fitting manners, then to take part in the liturgy distributed to them. And he says thus in the Numbers… having written thus: ‘For if the blood of goats and bulls, and ash of a heifer sprinkling those who have been shared sanctifies toward the cleanness of the flesh, by how much more the blood of Christ’; and true is the word. For if in the types is the benefiting, and the shadow saving, how would not rather the true—that is, the blood of Christ? So then water of purification the mixed with the ash of the heifer of the so-called putting-to-death of Christ a

title: Baptism burial; nekrosis = dead to world; haircut mind; wash garments works
english: Cyril: …clear symbol it was, as at least in the holy baptism we ourselves also pray to fulfill through faith. For as somewhere again all-divine Paul himself said, ‘For we have been buried-together with him through the baptism unto the death, that just as Christ was raised through the glory of the Father, so also we may walk in newness of life.’ And he said again: ‘Always carrying around the putting-to-death of Jesus in the body, that also the life of Jesus may be manifested in our mortal flesh.’
Palladius: And what then is the putting-to-death of Christ said here?

Cyril: The having died to world and sins, and to live through a sacred and holy and as-much-as-possible God-beloved life, upon which again Paul was being very solemnized saying: ‘For I through law died to law, that I may live to God; I have been co-crucified with Christ. And I no longer live, and Christ lives in me. And what I now live in flesh, I live in faith of the Son of God who has loved me, and handed himself over for me.’ This, I think, is… according to law. So then the removal of hairs hints the cleansing of mind, which the divine and sharper word of God would work in us. And washing-off of garments shows for us a bright and unadulterated citizenship, the outwardly-appearing. ‘For taking-thought good things, not only before Lord,’ according to what has been written, ‘but also before humans.’ And he himself somewhere says: ‘Let your light shine before the humans, that they may see your good

title: Inside/out pure; two calves = Christ; laying-on of hands before people
english: Cyril: …works, and may glorify your Father the in the heavens.’ So then it is necessary for those truly holy and sacred to be, from within and from without purely carrying around the putting-to-death of Jesus in their own body, and having been composed with him somehow through the holy baptism.
Palladius: You have spoken well.

Cyril: And he said a sacrifice for them must be brought forward in two calves, both perfect and yearling—that is, both soft and new; and perfect is the unto whole-burnt-offering, with fine flour soaked with oil being incense-burned-together with it; and the other at least, for sin is burned outside the camp; for thus the victims for sin are perfected. And again in both is Christ, in a calf at least the unto whole-burning, wholly holy, and unto a smell of fragrance for us to God and Father bringing for the saints the thankful and cheerful of the life in hope; for oil-soaked fine flour was being brought up together with the calf; and it will follow somehow altogether those who have honored the life in Christ… peoples vote for those being called of Christ, voicing very well that they would be worthy; and this in Churches, just as indeed also the ancients, beside the sacred and divine tent, were doing the hand-layings upon the Levites. So then clear that if neither in a church, nor indeed upon a people a hand-appointment should come to be, it will be beside the divine will, and outside sacred laws. And with the Levites having been perfected, they take hold of all the things unto sacred-work.
notes_covered: Num 8 laying on hands / church ordination
translator_notes: Levite ordination public; ends into Amen warning §29.

title: Close: only holy in Christ may touch the divine altars—Amen
english: Cyril: So then who is not holy in Christ and if he should not pre-purify, according to whichever manner would be fitting, let him depart far; for not without-penalty will he touch the divine altars.
Palladius: You have spoken most uprightly.
Cyril: To God the glory unto the ages, Amen.
translator_notes: Book 11 CLOSEOUT 29/29; short PG column kept.
